title: Identification and characterisation of capidermicin, a novel bacteriocin produced by Staphylococcus capitis.
source_review_depth: linked APD6/DBAASP/CAMP sequence and assay rows

materials_exhausted.supplementary_note: Landed supplementary assets are HTML/landing pages or figure/table download pages, not scientific XLSX/PDF supplemental datasets; no supplemental activity/toxicity table was recoverable or needed after primary Table 2 repair.

per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_1_database: DBAASP assay rows for seven Table 2 MIC values now match primary source rows and are source_verified; Staphylococcus epidermidis no-value database annotations are preserved as source_conflict cautions.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_2_activity_toxicity: Table 2 was reparsed manually into seven MIC records with target organism/strain, raw mass and molar values, units, method conditions, replicate statement, and XML/PDF locators.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_3_mechanism: Peptide identity/classification and stability are source-supported; proposed membrane permeabilization is retained as homology/structure inference rather than direct mechanism.
per_layer_decision_rationale.supplementary_materials: Local landed supplementary assets were opened as HTML/landing/download pages; no true supplementary spreadsheet/PDF activity table was present locally.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Staphylococcus epidermidis appears as an indicator strain in Table 1 but no Table 2 MIC value or CIT060 inhibited-indicator claim supports a positive MIC row.

Exact ORF4 peptide sequence is image-located in Fig 3B and cross-checked against merged sequence catalogs; XML/PDF text provides the 153 bp ORF, MN234131, TTG start, mass, and figure locator rather than machine-readable sequence text.
Discussion uses structural similarity to LnqQ/A53 to infer possible membrane permeabilization; ontology keeps this below direct_mechanism.

adjudication_summary: Source-reviewed rework repaired the Table 2 MIC matrix, reconciled linked database rows, and replaced automated mechanism placeholders with bounded ontology claims. The paper is accepted_with_cautions because database rows still contain unsupported Staphylococcus epidermidis activity annotations and the mechanism claim is inferred, not directly assayed.
